statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON (green). CME equity index futures have been halted since Friday's 21:00Z weekly settlement, so the entire published 24-hour window covers a closed market in which no Nasdaq-100 price path can develop.
recommendation: Tail is held at a weekend floor and no danger window is published, because the forecast horizon contains no U.S. cash session, no CME futures session and no scheduled U.S. macro release. The scores describe deferred gap and headline risk rather than observable intraday structure. Existing-position management and emergency protection rules are unaffected by this assessment. The first genuine repricing checkpoint is the Sunday 22:00Z futures reopen, which falls outside this window; the first scheduled U.S. checkpoint is the Dallas Fed Manufacturing Index on Monday at 14:30Z.
headline: Weekend halt holds after a hawkish-Warsh Friday: NQ settled 29,509.50 with equity volatility contained and the repricing carried by yields
body: Fed Chair Kevin Warsh's Jackson Hole keynote on Friday reset September policy expectations, with market-implied odds of a rate increase rising to roughly 56-59% from about 35% beforehand after he described inflation as still too high and the labour market as effectively at full employment. The repricing was expressed mainly in rates: the 10-year Treasury yield closed at 4.72%, up about 4.8bp on the day, with the 2-year near 4.34%. Equity damage stayed contained and internally split. Cash NDX closed at 29,433.43, down 0.70%, inside a 29,383.92-29,752.78 range, and NQ futures settled the week at 29,509.50, down 0.63%, inside 29,436.75-29,811.50; both finished in the lower part of their session ranges, but the decline was rotational rather than broad, with semiconductors giving back much of Thursday's Nvidia-led advance while other large-cap index members held up better. VIX eased to 14.43 from 14.51 within a 14.13-14.84 range, so implied volatility did not confirm a stress event. Energy remained a stabilising input, with WTI near $83.44 and Brent near $88.29 after a roughly 4% weekly decline, and reported Iran-Oman maritime-corridor contacts point away from a fresh supply discontinuity despite the long-running Strait of Hormuz conflict. The published window now covers a fully halted market: CME equity index futures do not reopen until 22:00Z on Sunday, which is outside this horizon, and no U.S. macro release is scheduled before Monday. Tail is therefore held at a weekend floor, since the persistent no-retracement path it measures requires continuous trading to form at all, while Stress decays to a low-20s overnight baseline and drifts back up through Saturday as the interval of unpriced weekend information widens. Confidence stays in the high band on complete verified Friday evidence and eases only as that observation ages. The shared Finviz cross-asset context was last collected well outside its 90-minute freshness bound and covers a session that has since settled, so this assessment rests on independently verified primary-source evidence.

lookbackSummary: The last 24 hours span the quiet pre-Jackson Hole overnight, the Warsh repricing itself, the weekly settlement and the first hours of the weekend halt. Overnight Asian and European hours held Tail near 11-12 with Stress around 50 and a mixed mode. Tail and Stress lifted through the U.S. morning as the speech reset September rate expectations, peaking at Tail 22 and Stress 64 in the 17:00Z hour with an event/whipsaw mode while yields rose. Price discovery stayed orderly: retracements occurred, VIX eased rather than spiked and the decline was rotational rather than broad, so Tail never approached the block threshold and the mapped state moved only between EA_ON and WATCH. Scores fell sharply into the 21:00Z settlement and again in the first halted hour, ending at Tail 7 and Stress 26. One clock hour, 10:00Z, has no published Claude assessment and is marked unavailable rather than reconstructed.
outlookSummary: The published window runs from the current hour through Saturday 22:00Z and contains no cash session, no CME futures session and no scheduled U.S. release. With no venue open, the pathological no-retracement path that Tail measures cannot form, so Tail is held at a 6-8 floor throughout and the mapped policy state stays EA_ON with no danger window. Stress decays from the mid-20s to a low-20s overnight baseline before drifting back up through Saturday as the interval of unpriced weekend information widens ahead of the Sunday 22:00Z reopen, which lies outside this horizon. Confidence starts at 85 and eases to 80 purely as the last live observation ages. Weekend Jackson Hole commentary and any Middle East development are treated as discovery for the reopening gap and would be verified against primary sources before affecting scoring.
